chunks: And with this chain, from al-Hasan, from his father al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala, from Abi 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Whoever recites 'Inna anzalnahu' (We sent it down) as an obligatory act among the obligations of Allah, an announcer will call out: O servant of Allah, Allah has forgiven you what has passed, so resume your deeds.

key_terms.إِنَّا أَنْزَلْنَاهُ: We sent it down (referring to the Quran or Laylat al-Qadr)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting Surah Al-Qadr as an act of worship?
ai.summary: In Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-Amal*, this hadith underscores the transformative power of reciting Surah Al-Qadr as a distinct act of worship, where a divine announcer declares the forgiveness of past sins. This spiritual renewal serves as a powerful motivator for the believer to 'start anew' in their deeds, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the interplay between divine mercy and continuous effort in spiritual purification. The narration highlights the unique status of this Surah, linking its recitation directly to the concept of *Tajdid al-Amal* (renewal of action) in the afterlife or daily devotion.
